channel.title: Wire — AI
channel.description: AI from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
item.description: Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking are our most advanced live dialogue models yet, built for natural conversation. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: There's a 100% Chance AI Agents Are Ruining the Internet
item.description: “AI agents” now have enough power and permission to be extremely annoying online. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Article: Your Next DSL Author Is a Language Model
item.description: In this article, the author introduces Typed Domain Grounding, an approach to reducing LLM hallucinations in domain-specific languages by embedding them in mainstream typed languages. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Presentation: Teaching Engineers, Trusting AI: How Education Enabled Autonomous Code Review
item.description: Sarah Deitke discusses how Duolingo drives cultural AI adoption beyond tooling access. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Dropbox Outlines How Focusing on Existing Infrastructure Efficiency Can Create Headroom for AI
item.description: Dropbox has outlined how a decade of infrastructure optimization is helping it absorb growing demand from AI without treating new data-center capacity as the only answer. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Maintaining the love for coding in the time of AI
AI-Assisted Discovery Helps Microsoft Patch More Than 1,000 Vulnerabilities in a Month
item.description: With its latest September 2026 Patch, which addresses more than 950 vulnerabilities, Microsoft has patched about 2,750 vulnerabilities so far this year. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: 1Password's AI patching benchmark is misleading
item.description: 1Password’s benchmark misrepresents AI patching. We share real-world data on human and agent patch quality from our consulting work and Patch the Planet and release two agent skills for testing and reviewing security fixes. (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: How much of F-Droid is LLM generated?
item.description: Investigating the use of LLMs in the Android FOSS community (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: I couldn't understand Dancing Links (DLX) as a finished algorithm, so I broke it down into an 8-step study sequence in Python
item.description: I came across Knuth's Dancing Links after naively thinking I could just code up a Sudoku Solver 😅and initially I made the mistake of trying to understand the finished implementation examples I found on the internet and from AI. (1 source: rprogramming)
